answer: A bond keyed to a hardware root, so one device cannot back two identities without spending the same key twice. Auditors rotate every epoch, and a panel drawing three jurors from one operator is voided and redrawn. That makes the sable alias expensive: real hardware, a fresh bond, a jury it cannot predict. The bridge between clone and payout stays narrow by design, and a reused device leaves an echo in the redraw log.
